verdict.rationale: Rive's own docs cover each element of the story. It has timeline and keyframe animation with interpolation, state machines that the runtime advances, and real-time data binding through view models, which serve as variables. It also supports interactivity that responds to user input, scrolling and application state, plus scripting for custom behavior. Rive frames this as building the shippable product rather than a mockup, which meets the goal of feeling like the real product. Missing for 10: explicit docs on state-machine transition conditions or logic, scroll-effect specifics beyond a one-line mention, and independent hands-on corroboration of prototyping use.

support.subject: As a designer, prototypes can carry advanced behavior — animation between states, conditions or variables, scroll effects — to feel like the real product

citations.quote: Bring your designs to life with timelines, keyframes, and smooth interpolation.
Build interactive experiences that respond to user input, screen size, scrolling, and application state.
Connect animations, text, colors, layouts, and other properties to real-time data.
State Machines with hundreds of states/layers
When data changes, your scene updates automatically.
Use scripting to create custom interactions, procedural animation, and behaviors that go beyond the built-in tools.
